fileHeader: Master prompt §9. Postgres via Prisma (SQLite in earlier revisions).
*Fee, *Tax, *Freight is an INTEGER in MINOR UNITS (paise for INR, cents
for USD). Never a float. The GST engine consumes and returns minor units
so rounding is explicit and testable (§11A.5a).
Exception: unitPrice* fields are Float, because component prices carry up
to 4 decimals. They are rounded to integer minor units at the line level
immediately, so float error never accumulates.
* ENUMS: enum-ish columns are String, with the authoritative union types +
Zod schemas in lib/domain/enums.ts. Kept as String rather than a native
Postgres enum because the permitted values change with business rules, and
a migration per value is a poor trade for a check the app already makes.
* PROVENANCE (§11A.0 rule 3): records that can be populated by an external
API carry provenance / provenanceActor / provenanceAt / provenanceRef.

models.name: User
models.doc: 1BUY's own people. Only two individuals represent 1BUY on paper and in correspondence — Ankit Sharma and Akash Dwivedi — so `title` carries the designation documents print ("VP", "MGR") while `role` stays the access dimension that gates the flow.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: Designation as printed on documents, e.g. "Vice President", "Manager".

fields.name: shipAddressLine1
fields.doc: Consignee / ship-to address on the supplier PO — a different dock to the registered billing address.

fields.name: contactAttn
fields.doc: "Attn" line printed on documents the supplier replies to.

fields.name: jurisdiction
fields.doc: Legal jurisdiction footer on the PO.

fields.name: poVoucherPrefix
fields.doc: Voucher-number prefix for supplier POs, e.g. "PO/SGSPL/26-27/".

models.name: GlossaryTerm
models.doc: Tooltip + glossary text lives in the DB so ops leads can edit it without a developer (§8.2). Nothing in the UI hardcodes a column tooltip.

fields.name: bankName
fields.doc: TT beneficiary details, printed on the supplier's proforma invoice.

fields.name: bankFeeNote
fields.doc: How wire charges are split, printed under the bank block.

models.name: AVLRecord
models.doc: Approved Vendor List. A supplier may only be selected on a Supplier PO when status = APPROVED and approvedUpto is in the future (§3.1b, AC#3).

models.name: HsnRate
models.doc: Date-effective GST rate master. The engine must look rates up by HSN + date and never hardcode 18% (§11A.5a).

fields.name: sourcingRef
fields.doc: The enquiry or sourcing reference this came from — the RFQ / Sourcing ID carried over from the sourcing step, which lives upstream of this platform. Free text on purpose: the format belongs to that system, not this one, and guessing a pattern would reject valid references.

fields.name: leadTimeDays
fields.doc: What the customer was promised, per line. Held on the line rather than the order because a mixed order can have one part on the shelf and another on a twelve-week lead.

fields.name: dateCodeLot
fields.doc: The date code or lot the customer requires, e.g. "2419+". This is a hard acceptance criterion on electronic components — the wrong date code is a rejected delivery, not a negotiation — so it is captured on their order and carried through to what we ask the supplier for.

fields.name: attention
fields.doc: "Attn" line — the named people at the receiving entity.

fields.name: shipmentMethod
fields.doc: e.g. "By air or courier nominated and paid by the buyer".

fields.name: originLocation
fields.doc: Where the goods ship from, printed as "From".

fields.name: destination
fields.doc: Where they are going, printed as "Destination".

fields.name: deliveryTime
fields.doc: Free text, because it is usually conditional on payment ("Within agreed 2–4 days after the seller's receipt of TT payment").

fields.name: paymentTerm
fields.doc: The payment term as written on the document, e.g. "100% TT in advance from the buyer to the seller before shipping."

fields.name: remarks
fields.doc: One remark per line, printed as a numbered list.

fields.name: sourcingRef
fields.doc: The enquiry or sourcing reference this came from — the RFQ / Sourcing ID carried over from the sourcing step, which lives upstream of this platform. Free text on purpose: the format belongs to that system, not this one, and guessing a pattern would reject valid references.

fields.name: voucherNo
fields.doc: Accounting voucher number, e.g. PO/SGSPL/26-27/0234. Distinct from poNumber: this is what the finance team quotes and what the supplier sees.

fields.name: referenceNo
fields.doc: The enquiry or quote bundle this order answers, printed as "Reference No. & Date".

fields.name: sourcingRef
fields.doc: The enquiry or sourcing reference this came from — the RFQ / Sourcing ID carried over from the sourcing step, which lives upstream of this platform. Free text on purpose: the format belongs to that system, not this one, and guessing a pattern would reject valid references.

fields.name: billToAddress
fields.doc: Registered billing address of the buying entity. Held per order because the entity may bill from a different registration than it ships to.

fields.name: dispatchedThrough
fields.doc: Carrier or hand-off named on the voucher; "—" when not yet nominated.

fields.name: destination
fields.doc: Final delivery point, e.g. "Bengaluru, KA · DAP".

fields.name: termsOfDelivery
fields.doc: The delivery term itself, e.g. CIP. Separate from `incoterms` because the voucher prints the agreed carriage term alongside the destination's own.

fields.name: termsAndConditions
fields.doc: One condition per line, printed as a numbered list.

models.name: POLinkMapping
models.doc: Customer PO line ↔ Supplier PO line allocation. Supports 1:1, partial allocation and split sourcing (§3.2).

fields.name: canonicalName
fields.doc: CustomerPO_1BUYPI_1BUYPO_SupplierPI — 4th segment is SPI-PENDING until the supplier PI is captured, then auto-completes and locks (§3.4).

fields.name: escrowFundedBy
fields.doc: Who funds the escrow and on what basis is NEGOTIATED per order in the terms between 1BUY and the supplier — it is not a platform-wide constant.

fields.name: escrowAgreedAmount
fields.doc: Set when escrowBasis = CUSTOM. Minor units.

models.name: StageTransition
models.doc: Immutable ledger of every stage change — powers the rail's hover detail, SLA ageing and the audit trail.

fields.name: documents
fields.doc: Proof of the movement — a bank advice for a deposit, a release instruction or signed authority for a payout. Tied to the transaction rather than the order, because "which payment does this prove" is the whole question.

models.name: EscrowApproval
models.doc: Final release requires two distinct Finance-role approvers (§11A.4, AC#23).

fields.name: exchangeRateUsed
fields.doc: Customs FX differs from the PO's locked rate — variance is surfaced (§11A.3)

fields.name: taxTreatment
fields.doc: INTRA_STATE (CGST+SGST) | INTER_STATE (IGST) | ZERO_RATED_SEZ | ZERO_RATED_EXPORT

fields.name: rateSourceId
fields.doc: Which HsnRate row produced these rates — powers "why is this number what it is" traceability (§11A.5 UI requirements).

fields.name: ewbNumber
fields.doc: Null until the number is obtained. The obligation to carry a way bill is created by the movement of goods, not by a portal being reachable, so the row exists from dispatch and the number is filled in after (Rule 138).

fields.name: validUntil
fields.doc: Validity runs from generation, so it is unknown while the number is.

models.name: InputTaxCredit
models.doc: Input Tax Credit ledger. Import IGST lands here and is EXCLUDED from landed cost; BCD/SWS never appear here and ARE included in landed cost (§9, AC#26).

models.name: ReverseChargeSelfInvoice
models.doc: Self-invoice for import of services (foreign lab / foreign freight agent) — records both the RCM liability and the corresponding credit (§11A.5a).

fields.name: storagePath
fields.doc: Where the uploaded bytes live on disk, relative to the storage root. Null for generated documents, which are rendered on demand rather than stored.

fields.name: stageId
fields.doc: Set when the file was attached as evidence for a particular stage.

fields.name: bodyText
fields.doc: Documents in the MVP are generated/simulated rather than uploaded binaries; bodyText holds renderable content so every doc opens to something real.

models.name: CommunicationContext
models.doc: The "context" requirement — no message floats without knowing which part of the order it concerns (§7.2).

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why the change was made, when a justification was required — a correction to a signed-off record, or an amendment to locked terms. Carried on EVERY row it justifies, because reading one row alone must explain itself.

models.name: StageEvidence
models.doc: What the team recorded to show a stage was genuinely fulfilled, before the order was allowed to move on. One row per work order per stage.  Evidence stays editable after the fact: a figure mistyped under time pressure has to be correctable, and the honest way to allow that is to keep every version rather than to lock the record. `revisions` is that history.

fields.name: stageId
fields.doc: One of the stage ids in lib/domain/stages.ts.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: The declared fields for this stage, as captured. Keyed by field id.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: SUBMITTED once every required field is answered; DRAFT while incomplete.

fields.name: completedAt
fields.doc: Set when the record first became complete.

models.name: StageEvidenceRevision
models.doc: Every save of a stage's evidence, kept in full. Corrections are visible as corrections — what changed, who changed it, and why.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: 1 for the first save, incrementing thereafter.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: The complete set of values as at this revision.

fields.name: changeSummary
fields.doc: Human-readable list of what changed from the previous revision.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Required when correcting an already-complete record.

models.name: CustomStage
models.doc: A step someone added to ONE work order's flow, between two standard stages.  The 39-stage ladder in lib/domain/stages.ts stays the single source of truth for the standard flow and is never mutated: real orders occasionally need a step the ladder does not model — a second inspection, a customer factory visit, a re-test after a repack — and inventing a global stage for a one-off would corrupt the ladder for every other order.  So these are per-order additions, layered on at render time and drawn distinctly, so nobody mistakes a local improvisation for standard process.

fields.name: afterStageId
fields.doc: The standard stage this sits immediately after.

fields.name: beforeStageId
fields.doc: The standard stage it sits immediately before — recorded so the insertion point survives even if the ladder's ordering is later revised.

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: Phase it renders inside, taken from the stage it follows.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why this order needed a step the standard flow does not have. Required: an unexplained extra step is indistinguishable from a mistake.

fields.name: owner
fields.doc: Who has to do it.

fields.name: exitCriteria
fields.doc: What has to be true to consider it finished.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: PENDING | DONE | SKIPPED

fields.name: blocking
fields.doc: When true the order should not pass this point until it is done. Advisory: the stage ladder still governs transitions, so this is a flag the flow surfaces rather than a hard gate that could deadlock an order.

fields.name: sequence
fields.doc: Ordering when several steps share the same insertion point.

fields.name: approval
fields.doc: PENDING_APPROVAL | APPROVED | REJECTED — the request state, separate from `status`, which is whether the step itself has been carried out.  Adding a step changes what "done" means for the order, so it is a request rather than an edit: somebody asks, somebody else agrees, and both are on the record. A step awaiting approval is visible on the flow but does not gate anything until it is approved.

fields.name: decidedBy
fields.doc: Who decided, when, and — for a rejection — why.

models.name: OrderPhasePlan
models.doc: One phase's place in a single work order's flow — the per-order overlay that lets the seven macro phases be reordered, or taken out of the flow entirely.  Rows exist only for an order whose flow has actually been re-planned. An order running the standard ladder stores nothing, so the common case costs nothing and "no rows" unambiguously means "standard flow" rather than "plan unknown". When rows do exist there are always seven of them, which makes the read a straight `orderBy: position` with no gaps to reason about.  The stage ladder itself is never touched. See lib/domain/phase-plan.ts for what may be moved, what may be dropped, and why.

fields.name: phase
fields.doc: A..G

fields.name: position
fields.doc: Zero-based position in this order's flow.

fields.name: skipped
fields.doc: Taken out of this order's flow. The stages stay visible on the rail, struck through, so what was cut is never invisible.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Why this phase was moved or dropped. Held per phase, not just in the audit log, so the rail can show the reason against the phase it belongs to.
